title: Bands form as atoms approach
text: Drag the spacing slider from 6 Å down to the 2.35 Å silicon bond length: isolated levels broaden into bands and a ~1.1 eV gap opens between the filled valence band and the empty conduction band.

title: Fermi–Dirac smearing with temperature
text: At 0 K the occupation is a sharp step at E_F. Raise the temperature and the step smears over a few kT; the tail above E_F is what puts electrons in the conduction band.

title: Metal, semiconductor, insulator
text: Same electrons, different band fillings: a half-filled band conducts, a full band below a small gap (Si, 1.12 eV) conducts a little when warm, a big gap (SiO₂, 9 eV) does not.

title: Intrinsic silicon
text: Pure silicon: n = p = n_i = 1.0×10¹⁰ cm⁻³ at 300 K and E_F sits very near midgap. Only about one atom in 5×10¹² has a free electron.

title: n-type silicon (phosphorus doped)
text: N_D = 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ donors: n ≈ N_D, holes drop to n_i²/n ≈ 10⁴ cm⁻³, and E_F moves up toward E_c. Apply a field and the electrons drift.

title: p-type silicon (boron doped)
text: N_A = 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ acceptors: holes are the majority carriers, E_F moves down toward E_v, and the current is carried by holes drifting along the field.

title: Carriers vs temperature
text: Follow the n(T) curve: at low T dopants freeze out, around room temperature n = N_D (extrinsic), at high T intrinsic pairs overwhelm the doping and n = p = n_i(T).

title: Dopant freeze-out
text: At 60 K there is too little thermal energy to ionise most donors (45 meV below E_c), so n is far below N_D.

title: Drift and diffusion currents
text: Electrons move opposite to the field (drift) and also flow from high to low concentration (diffusion). Each gives a current; Einstein’s relation D = μkT/q links them.

title: Compensated doping
text: Both donors and acceptors present: they cancel, leaving net doping N_D − N_A. Mobility is reduced because all ionised impurities scatter carriers.

title: PN junction at equilibrium
text: N_A = N_D = 10¹⁶ cm⁻³: V_bi = 0.714 V and the depletion width is 0.43 µm. Diffusion and drift balance; E_F is flat.

title: Forward bias
text: At +0.65 V the barrier shrinks to V_bi − V, the depletion region narrows and the current rises exponentially (use the log-I axis to see the 60 mV/decade slope).

title: Reverse bias
text: At −5 V the depletion region widens to 1.1 µm, the junction capacitance falls and only a tiny leakage current (generation in the depletion region) flows.

title: Reverse breakdown
text: With 10¹⁷ cm⁻³ on both sides the peak field reaches the critical value near −11 V and the current shoots up (avalanche). The series resistance finally limits it.

title: Depletion approximation vs numeric Poisson
text: The dashed lines are the depletion approximation; the solid cyan lines solve Poisson’s equation numerically with carrier statistics. They agree well except for the rounded edges.

title: One-sided junction (p⁺n)
text: N_A = 10¹⁸ ≫ N_D = 10¹⁵: the depletion region sits almost entirely in the lightly doped n side, so its width, capacitance and breakdown are set by N_D. Note how the numeric solution deviates where the heavily doped side is thinner than a Debye length.

title: LED colours from bandgaps
text: InGaN: more indium means a smaller gap and a longer wavelength — from violet through blue to green. Move the composition slider and watch the photon colour change.

title: Infrared LED (GaAs)
text: GaAs has E_g = 1.42 eV, so its photons (870 nm) are invisible to the eye: the LED in your remote control.

title: Why silicon is a poor LED
text: Silicon has an indirect bandgap: recombination needs a phonon too, so almost all pairs recombine without light (EQE ~10⁻⁴), and its 1.12 eV photons are infrared anyway.

title: Solar cell I–V
text: Under 1 sun the diode curve shifts into the fourth quadrant. Read off V_oc ≈ 0.63 V, I_sc ≈ 40 mA/cm², the max-power point (blue rectangle) and the fill factor.

title: Solar cell under dim light
text: At 0.1 sun the current drops tenfold but V_oc only falls by ~60 mV (logarithmic), so efficiency holds up reasonably.

title: Parasitic resistances
text: Add series resistance (R_s = 4 Ω·cm²) and the fill factor collapses; lower the shunt resistance to see the slope near I_sc.

title: Zener voltage regulator
text: A 5.1 V Zener clamps the output at V_Z while the input varies from 6 V upwards: the flat part of the V_out–V_in curve.

title: Avalanche Zener (9.1 V)
text: Above about 7 V breakdown is by avalanche multiplication, with a sharper knee than a low-voltage tunnelling Zener.

title: BJT output characteristics
text: Each curve is a fixed base current; the nearly flat parts are the active region (current source), the steep start is saturation. The dashed load line picks the operating point Q.

title: BJT in the active region
text: I_B = 20 µA, β = 100 → I_C ≈ 2 mA. The base–emitter barrier is lowered; the collector junction is strongly reverse biased and sweeps injected electrons away.

title: BJT in saturation
text: With a big base current and a large R_C the transistor cannot supply β·I_B: V_CE collapses to ~0.2 V, the collector junction turns on and the gain falls — a closed switch.

title: BJT in cutoff
text: With no base current both junctions are off and (almost) no collector current flows: an open switch with V_CE = V_CC.

title: MOS capacitor: accumulation, depletion, inversion
text: Sweep V_GS from −1 V upward and watch the band diagram: holes accumulate, then are depleted, and above V_T the surface inverts (E_c approaches E_F) and an electron layer forms.

title: MOSFET output curves and pinch-off
text: Increase V_DS: the channel tapers and pinches off at V_DS = V_GS − V_T; beyond it the current is nearly constant (saturation).

title: MOSFET transfer curve and subthreshold slope
text: Switch on the log axis: below V_T the current falls exponentially, about 60 mV per decade — the physical limit of the turn-off slope at room temperature.

title: Short-channel effects
text: At L = 50 nm velocity saturation lowers V_dsat and the current is no longer quadratic; the drain also lowers the barrier (DIBL) and the output curves tilt upward.

title: FinFET and gate-all-around
text: Wrapping the gate around a thin fin or nanosheets shortens the electrostatic scale length λ, so DIBL stays small even at 20 nm gate lengths where the planar device has lost control.

title: CMOS inverter transfer curve
text: The steep transition at V_M gives gain > 1 and defines the noise margins; the load-line panel shows nMOS and pMOS curves intersecting at V_out.

title: Inverter switching
text: Watch the input toggle and the output charge or discharge the load capacitor through the on-transistor; only during the transition do both conduct briefly.

title: NAND gate
text: Series nMOS pull-down, parallel pMOS pull-up: the output is low only when both inputs are high. Toggle A and B.

title: NOR gate
text: Parallel nMOS, series pMOS: the output is high only when both inputs are low.

title: Dynamic power and voltage scaling
text: P = α·C·V²·f: lowering V_DD from 1.2 V to 0.8 V cuts dynamic power by more than half at the same frequency — but delay grows as V_DD approaches V_T.

title: CMOS fabrication step by step
text: Auto-play walks through a simplified process: oxidation, polysilicon, lithography, etch, implant, dielectric, planarisation and copper wiring.

title: Lithography
text: UV light through a photomask exposes the resist everywhere except under the chrome; the pattern becomes a 40 nm gate.

title: Ion implantation
text: The gate blocks the ions, so the source and drain are automatically aligned to the gate (self-alignment).
